newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines plans export of 200,000 tonnes sugar.
newsitem.headline: Philippines plans export of 200,000 tonnes sugar.

text.p: The Philippines plans to export 200,000 tonnes of refined sugar in the world market to reduce its mounting stocks, Sugar Regulatory Administration chief Wilson Gamboa said on Tuesday.
Gamboa told reporters the Philippines, to reduce its sugar glut, had also sought to advance shipment of its remaining sugar export quota to the United States.
"We have to decongest our inventory," he said. Gamboa pegged the country's existing sugar stocks at 700,000 tonnes.
Local sugar farmers and millers have been complaining of the slide in sugar prices due to the importation of some 1.2 million tonnes from September 1995 to July this year.
Philippine sugar prices slid to 500 pesos per 50-kilo bag from 800 pesos last year, they said.
Gamboa said the start of the milling season for the current crop year would further boost the country's sugar stocks.
Local millers are expected to churn out an additional 1.2 million metric tonnes between December 1996 and March 1997, he said.
Gamboa said he was confident the United States would approve the Philippine request to ship its remaining 141,000 tonnes.
The Philippines has so far exported 78,000 tonnes since the start of its 1996-1997 crop year ending August. It has an allocation of 219,000 tonnes of sugar to the United States.
The Philippines is a beneficiary of a programme under which the U.S. pays premium prices for sugar imports from developing countries.
